name: web-accessibility
rationale: MeaBeclick UX owns accessible, child-friendly interaction requirements for a phone-first Hebrew product, while its installed inventory has broad design guidance but no dedicated accessibility evidence workflow. This candidate adds WCAG-informed interaction contracts, keyboard and focus checks, assistive-technology evidence, and bounded release criteria without replacing Engineering implementation verification.
risks: Some routing links point to sibling skills not installed in this profile; mitigate by using the self-contained accessibility workflow and consulting current official framework documentation where those optional siblings are absent.
The skill correctly avoids claiming WCAG conformance from automation alone, so release reviews still require scoped manual keyboard, accessibility-tree, and supported assistive-technology evidence.
summary: Defines WCAG 2.2-informed accessibility requirements, implementation contracts, and evidence-based release checks for web interfaces.
